record.original_question: Study binary operations that preserve random strings or random sequences.

evidence.quote: Study binary operations which preserve random strings/sequences.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A binary string is an element of $\{0,1\}^*$ and a binary sequence is an element of $\{0,1\}^\omega$. The plain Kolmogorov complexity $C(x)$ of a finite string $x$ is the length of a shortest input to a fixed universal Turing machine that outputs $x$; the prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity $K(x)$ is defined analogously using a universal prefix-free machine. A finite string $x$ is called (Kolmogorov) random if $K(x) \ge |x| - O(1)$. An infinite binary sequence $X \in \{0,1\}^\omega$ is Martin-Löf random if there is a constant $c$ such that $K(X{\restriction}n) \ge n - c$ for all $n$, equivalently if $X$ avoids every Martin-Löf test (every uniformly c.e. sequence $\{U_n\}_{n\in\omega}$ of open subsets of $\{0,1\}^\omega$ with $\mu(U_n) \le 2^{-n}$).

Problem. Characterize the computable binary operations $\ast : \{0,1\}^* \times \{0,1\}^* \to \{0,1\}^*$ (respectively, $\ast : \{0,1\}^\omega \times \{0,1\}^\omega \to \{0,1\}^\omega$) that preserve randomness, in the following sense:

(a) For finite strings: identify the computable binary operations $\ast$ such that there is a constant $c$ for which, whenever $x$ and $y$ are random strings (in the sense above) of suitable lengths, the string $x \ast y$ satisfies $K(x \ast y) \ge |x \ast y| - c$.

(b) For infinite sequences: identify the computable binary operations $\ast$ such that whenever $X, Y \in \{0,1\}^\omega$ are Martin-Löf random, $X \ast Y$ is Martin-Löf random; and more generally describe the joint conditions on $(X,Y)$ (such as mutual relative randomness) under which $X \ast Y$ is Martin-Löf random.

Give a complete classification of such operations, or natural sufficient and necessary conditions on $\ast$ that guarantee preservation of randomness.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known: Van Lambalgen's theorem characterizes the join operation (X ⊕ Y is Martin-Löf random iff X is ML-random and Y is ML-random relative to X), and there is a substantial literature on randomness preservation under computable measure-preserving maps and on van Lambalgen-style independence. However, a general classification of binary operations preserving randomness of strings or sequences does not appear to be settled, so the problem in its full generality appears open / unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmically random sequence - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Van Lambalgen's theorem: α ⊕ β is Martin-Löf random iff α is ML-random and β is ML-random relative to α.
status_evidence.claim: A specific binary operation (the join) has a known characterization of when it preserves randomness, but general classifications are not stated.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmic Randomness (Downey)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys randomness preservation, van Lambalgen's theorem, and effective dimension; no general classification of randomness-preserving binary operations is given.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem of classifying binary operations preserving randomness is not resolved in standard surveys.
